summative_rubric.title: Data Detectives Return — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 to score against all 5 expectations on a 4-level scale.

rows.expectation_text: sort sets of data about people or things according to two attributes, using tables and logic diagrams, including Venn and Carroll diagrams

levels.descriptor: Sorts by one attribute only. Cannot use Venn or Carroll.
Sorts by 2 attributes with prompts using either Venn OR Carroll.
Independently sorts by 2 attributes using both Venn and Carroll diagrams correctly.
Sorts by 3 attributes (3-circle Venn) and explains when to use Venn vs Carroll.

rows.expectation_text: collect data through observations, experiments, and interviews to answer questions of interest that focus on two pieces of information, and organize the data in two-way tally tables

levels.descriptor: Cannot ask 2 questions independently. Tally in wrong cell.
Asks 2 questions with prompts. Tally with single-cell rule with prompts.
Independently asks 2 questions, surveys 6+, tallies 1-cell-per-child correctly.
Surveys 10+, totals rows + columns accurately.

rows.expectation_text: display sets of data, using one-to-one correspondence, in concrete graphs, pictographs, line plots, and bar graphs with proper sources, titles, and labels

levels.descriptor: Bar heights don't match counts. No title or labels.
Bar heights mostly match. Title or labels missing.
Bar heights match exactly. Title and labels both present.
Bar graph + line plot or pictograph (multiple displays).

rows.expectation_text: identify the mode(s), if any, for various data sets presented in concrete graphs, pictographs, line plots, bar graphs, and tables, and explain what this measure indicates about the data

levels.descriptor: Cannot identify the mode.
Identifies single mode with prompts.
Independently identifies mode in bar graphs and tally tables. Recognizes no-mode and bimodal cases.
Explains why mode matters: 'mode tells us what's most popular'.

rows.expectation_text: analyse different sets of data presented in various ways, including in logic diagrams, line plots, and bar graphs, by asking and answering questions about the data and drawing conclusions, then make convincing arguments and informed decisions

levels.descriptor: Personal preference instead of data conclusion.
Group conclusion with sentence frame.
Independent group conclusion using mode.
Comparison conclusion + informed decision based on data.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during and after Lesson 5 capstone. Level 3 is the grade-level expectation.

summative_task_script.title: Bar Graph Case Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties Lesson 5 capstone, the 5 detective steps, and the rubric together.
administration_steps: Before: photocopy templates, print rubric, ready Junior Data Detective certificates.
Step 1-2 (Ask + Tally, 5 min): question + 2-way table for 6 classmates. Evidence for D1.1, D1.2.
Step 3 (Bar graph, 8 min): build from tally. Evidence for D1.3.
Step 4 (Mode, 5 min): find the mode. Evidence for D1.4.
Step 5 (Conclude, 5 min): write conclusion. Evidence for D1.5.
After: review with each child. Below-Level-3 needs targeted small-group work.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the Capstone Template as primary evidence.

evidence_per_expectation.D1.1: Look at the 2-way tally — child sorted by 2 questions consistently.
evidence_per_expectation.D1.2: Look at the 2-way tally — single-tally per child, totals correct.
evidence_per_expectation.D1.3: Look at the bar graph — bar heights match tally totals; title + labels present.
evidence_per_expectation.D1.4: Look at the mode line — child identified the value with the highest count.
evidence_per_expectation.D1.5: Look at the conclusion sentence — uses GROUP language and references the MODE.
